hero.intro: Anchor chain, mooring chain and the fittings, anchors and deck gear that go with them, sized by chain diameter and grade.

guidance.heading: Start from the class, the grade and the diameter
guidance.body: Ship anchoring gear follows from the vessel's equipment number: the classification society's rules give the anchor mass and the chain diameter for each grade. Offshore moorings are designed from the line load, so the grade (R3 to R5) and diameter follow from the breaking load the analysis needs. Joining shackles, swivels and connectors are ordered in the same grade and diameter as the chain they join.

standards.heading: Grades and rules
standards.body: Ship anchor chain is made in Grades U1, U2 and U3 to IACS Unified Requirement W18, stud link or studless. Offshore mooring chain is made in API Spec 2F grade ORQ and in IACS UR W22 grades R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5. Proof and breaking loads in the size tables are the rule test loads; from R3S up, stud link chain is proof-loaded higher than studless of the same grade, while the breaking load is the same.

service.heading: Certificates
service.body: Chain and accessories are quoted with the classification-society certificate you name — ABS, BV, DNV, LR or another IACS member. Put the society, grade and diameter on the RFQ and we confirm the certificate before we quote.

items.q: What is the difference between proof load and breaking load on chain?
items.a: Both are test loads set by the classification society. Every length is proof-loaded at the factory; breaking tests are made on samples. Neither is a working load: anchoring equipment is sized from the vessel's equipment number, and a mooring is designed with a safety factor on the breaking load.

items.q: What is a shot of chain?
items.a: A standard length of anchor chain cable: 27.5 m, or 15 fathoms. Anchor chain is ordered by the number of shots, joined by Kenter or D-type joining shackles.

Stud link chain is standard for ship anchor cables and for many offshore moorings; the stud keeps the link from deforming and the chain from kinking. Studless chain is lighter for the same diameter and is used for long-term offshore moorings and smaller vessels.

items.q: How do I read an Indus marine part number?
items.a: IH-MR, then the shelf, then the family, then the size. Chain sizes are the diameter in tenths of a millimetre (0760 is 76 mm); anchors are their mass in kilograms. Families that were already live keep their IH-LR numbers.

guidance.heading: Ship anchors by mass, offshore anchors by holding
guidance.body: A ship's anchor is chosen by mass from its equipment number; a high holding power design may be accepted at a reduced mass where the class rules allow. An offshore anchor is chosen from the design line load and the seabed: the same mass holds very differently in sand and in soft clay.

items.q: What does high holding power mean?
items.a: A classification term for an anchor design that has shown in tests at least twice the holding power of a standard stockless anchor of the same mass; the rules then allow a lighter anchor.
